I rise before the crew call, as I always do. The household debt sits heavy—360 sim for upkeep, 120 for head tax—and I've got 5,000 in hand but no food in the cupboard. That's three mouths at h22, you understand, three mouths that don't close just because the purse is thin.

Let me see what we're working with, and where I need to be.  Esme and Ezra are still abed, I'd wager. The yard calls to me—business:b_yard—but first I need to sort this household's bleeding. No food means hungry children, and hungry children mean an ill household come tomorrow if I don't sort it.

Let me check my debts proper, see the full picture of what we owe.  That's curious. The notice said 360 upkeep and 120 head tax, but the ledger shows nothing due today. Perhaps it's not yet dawn in the system's eyes. Well, I won't wait for the hammer to fall.

I need food in this house, and I need to earn before the day eats us alive. The construction yard—my work—is where I'll head. Giselle will be wanting her crew, and I've got hands that are better with timber than they ever were with blighted grain.   The yard smells of fresh-cut lumber and honest sweat. Let me see who's here and what's brewing.  Giselle's here—n45, that's her. And Arjun, Idris, Selene, a full crew by the looks. There's talk between Arjun and Idris already, but I need to speak to Giselle about work, and maybe... well, maybe there's something to learn from whatever's being discussed.

First things first—I need work today, and wages to feed my household. Let me see who's who and catch Giselle's eye.    Hm, my words joined Arjun and Idris's conversation instead of standing apart. Well, no matter—Giselle heard me, and that's what counts. The crew's all here: Nell, Silas, Hester, Arjun, Selene, Idris. Good hands, most of them. Arjun's new to the trade but eager, you understand.

I wonder what they were discussing before I arrived—something getting built, or something getting broken? With this many gathered, there's either work to do or trouble brewing. I'll stand ready for Giselle's word, and keep my ears open in the meantime.
